content.title: About
content.content: Nachos are crunchy corn chips, usually served with salsa, guacamole, cheese sauce or other dips. They are made from corn flour, water and salt, shaped into triangles or half‑circles and fried until golden and crisp.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nachos were invented in the Mexican town of Piedras Negras in 1943 when chef Ignacio "Nacho" Anaya created a dish from leftover tortilla chips and melted cheese.
The classic cheese sauce is made from processed cheese, milk and spices, but today versions with cheddar, Monterey Jack or even vegan cheeses are common.
Corn chips can be plain or seasoned with chili, paprika, lime, garlic and onion powders.
In the United States more than 1 billion bags of nachos are sold each year, while in Mexico they are often served as "nachos con carne" (chips topped with beef, beans and cheese).
There are "healthier" nachos made from whole‑grain or sweet‑potato flour, offering more fiber and nutrients.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Corn chips provide steady energy through slowly digestible carbohydrates, useful for active lifestyles.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain versions are rich in fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Corn contains carotenoids such as lutein and zeaxanthin, which promote eye health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Nachos provide thiamine, niacin and folate, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They also supply magnesium and iron, important for muscle function and blood formation.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Most packaged nachos are salty, which can raise blood pressure if eaten frequently.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Chips are high in calories and fat, so portion control is recommended, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Trans fats in some brands
items.content: Certain nachos are fried in partially hydrogenated oils that contain trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of people are allergic to corn and may experience skin or digestive reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Nachos are served as a snack, paired with salsa, guacamole, cheese sauce, beans, beef, chicken or vegetables. They can be baked with cheese and spices for a loaded nachos casserole. For a lighter option, choose whole‑grain or sweet‑potato chips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep nachos in an airtight bag in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer them to a sealed container to maintain crispness. For long‑term storage they can be refrigerated, but avoid moisture.

content.title: About
content.content: Doritos Cool Ranch tortilla chips are crunchy corn chips coated with a seasoning blend that combines buttermilk, onion, garlic and herb notes. The product is manufactured by Frito‑Lay and sold in various package sizes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Cool Ranch flavor was first introduced in the United States in the early 1990s and quickly became one of Doritos’ top-selling varieties.
The seasoning contains dried milk powder, which gives the characteristic creamy taste.
Doritos is a brand owned by PepsiCo, with corn chip production taking place at multiple facilities worldwide.
Packaging typically lists calorie and sodium content, helping consumers monitor their intake.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Corn chips provide carbohydrates that deliver quick energy.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Corn contributes dietary fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Small amounts of vitamins B1, B3 and B6 are present, participating in metabolism.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The salty seasoning makes the snack high in sodium, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Tortilla chips are calorie‑dense; excessive consumption can contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product may contain dairy and gluten, important for individuals with allergies.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the chips as a standalone snack, with dips, in salads, or as a crunchy topping for Mexican‑style dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place and reseal the package after opening to keep the chips crisp and prevent moisture absorption.
